page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. This CPU provides 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. This hardware profile delivers high resource density for compute-heavy workloads, offering a balanced trade-off between high-speed DDR5 memory and dense multi-core processing without the overhead of local storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8i.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks. The hardware-accelerated instruction sets enable top-tier performance in cryptography, database operations, and software compilation. It also delivers top-tier prompt processing speeds for small, medium, and large language models. This profile is optimized for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
